purpose: Curated plant-health evidence registry for dr-plant. Records are references and research leads, not diagnostic training labels unless explicitly validated.

rules.promotion: A finding may be used as diagnostic evidence only after expert review, symptom verification, image provenance and license checks.
rules.socialMedia: Social-media posts are leads only. Never treat captions or comments as confirmed diagnoses.
rules.images: Do not copy or redistribute images until their license or explicit permission is verified.
rules.uncertainty: Keep suspected, reported, and confirmed findings separate.

diseases.scientificName: Plant nutritional disorder (specific nutrient and causal factor undetermined)
diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead expanded from grapevine to trees generally. Nutrient deficiency can affect many tree crops, including fruit trees, but visible patterns and susceptibility vary by species and cultivar. Yellowing is a symptom, not a nutrient diagnosis. Nitrogen deficiency often causes more uniform paling of older leaves; iron or manganese deficiency may cause interveinal chlorosis on young leaves; magnesium and potassium patterns often begin on older foliage, but patterns vary by crop. Similar symptoms can result from unsuitable soil pH, salinity, waterlogging/drought, root injury or disease, and nutrient excess or imbalance. Do not diagnose a specific element or recommend fertilizer from a photograph alone. Use crop-specific interpretation with soil and/or leaf-tissue analysis and field context.

diseases.scientificName: Venturia oleaginea (syn. Spilocaea oleagina; anamorph name)
diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location, cultivar, season, specimen and expert confirmation were not specified. Typical symptoms are circular brown/olive-green to gray or dark spots, often with concentric rings and a yellow halo, mainly on the upper leaf surface. Severe/recurrent infection can cause chlorosis and premature leaf fall, especially in humid lower canopy. Infection is favored by prolonged leaf wetness, rain/high humidity and mild temperatures. Some infections may remain latent for months; absence of visible spots does not exclude infection. Do not diagnose from yellowing alone; microscopy or suitable laboratory testing can confirm.

diseases.scientificName: Non-specific symptom / abiotic or biotic disorder; causal agent undetermined
diseases.applicability: User reports this symptom on walnut (Juglans spp.) and loquat (Eriobotrya japonica). Treat these host associations as field leads, not independently confirmed host-specific diagnoses. Interpret separately for each crop.
diseases.notes: User-described symptom: leaf margins and tips dry, turn brown and become brittle, sometimes progressing inward. This is marginal leaf necrosis/leaf scorch, a symptom pattern rather than one disease. Differential causes include drought or inadequate water uptake, hot/drying wind and heat, salinity or fertilizer-salt injury, unsuitable nutrient status, waterlogging/root injury or root rot, and some vascular pathogens. Loquat references list water deficit/excess, salinity and nutrient/mineral disorders among environmental problems; this does not establish a single cause. Walnut blight more typically causes small dark-brown spots with yellowish-green halos on leaves and can affect other green tissues; do not equate it with uniform marginal scorch. Compare distribution across canopy and trees, recent weather/irrigation/fertilizer/spray history, root-zone drainage, and presence of spots/lesions or branch dieback. Do not diagnose Xylella or any pathogen from marginal browning alone; pathogen confirmation requires appropriate laboratory testing. No treatment or fertilizer recommendation from a photograph alone.

diseases.notes: A crop-specific reference for citrus scab, especially relevant to lemon. Typical symptoms include small elevated pale-orange to pink/gray lesions that become raised, corky, wart-like protuberances on leaves and fruit; young leaves may become distorted and severely affected young fruit may be misshapen. This record is not evidence of current occurrence in Syria or any particular orchard. Distinguish sour citrus scab caused by E. fawcettii from sweet orange scab caused by E. australis; laboratory or qualified plant-health assessment may be needed for uncertain cases. No image labels or local prevalence claims are inferred.

diseases.notes: Reference for grape-leaf differential diagnosis. French INRAE ePhytia and university extension references describe round to polygonal tan/brown necrotic leaf spots with darker margins; small black pycnidia may become visible in mature lesions. The pathogen can also affect canes and bunches, but cane and bunch symptoms must remain separate image-organ tasks from leaf classification. Leaf spots overlap with other grape disorders, so a photograph alone is not definitive. The French reference describes European occurrence but does not establish occurrence or prevalence on the Syrian coast. diseases.scientificName: Multiple fungi (Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, Phaeoacremonium aleophilum, Fomitiporia mediterranea)
diseases.notes: Esca is a multifactorial grapevine trunk-disease syndrome, not a single leaf pathogen. Foliar expression can include irregular interveinal discoloration and necrosis with a tiger-stripe appearance; an apoplectic form can cause sudden whole-vine wilting and leaf drying, often in summer after rain followed by heat. INRAE describes associated wood symptoms such as white soft rot and central or sectorial brown necrosis, and multiple associated fungi including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, Phaeoacremonium spp. and Fomitiporia mediterranea. Do not infer Esca from a leaf photograph alone: inspect trunk/cordon context and seek expert or laboratory assessment. The linked French field reference is not evidence of local coastal-Syria prevalence.

diseases.notes: A grapevine eriophyid mite pest, not a fungal disease. The erineum strain produces roundish warty swellings on the upper leaf surface and corresponding discolored, felt-like patches (erinea) on the underside. The mites are minute (about 0.25 mm), and UC IPM notes that several strains occur and may represent different species; visible symptoms support a pest differential but do not always settle species identity. Keep this distinct from Tetranychid spider mites, thrips and fungal mildews. No Syrian coastal occurrence is asserted.

Greening and scale labels should not be treated as confirmed causal diagnoses without checking the original annotation protocol. No images were downloaded or copied.
datasets.licenseEvidence: Mendeley Data landing page lists CC BY 4.0; file-level review remains pending.

datasets.name: PlantVillage (unaugmented reference release)
datasets.license: Unresolved for the exact image package used here. The official GitHub repository has no visible LICENSE file; third-party mirrors report conflicting terms. Do not download/reuse until the original Mendeley record and exact package terms are verified.
datasets.intendedUse: Controlled-image classification baseline and label-map reference only; not a field-generalization benchmark.
datasets.region: United States / source institution Penn State; precise image acquisition locations not fully represented in the supplied metadata
datasets.imageTask: Leaf-level image classification; mostly controlled/simple backgrounds. Not fruit, bunch, or lesion segmentation.
datasets.sourceAudit: GitHub README reports 54,306 images, 14 crop species and 26 diseases; TensorFlow Datasets catalog reports 54,303 examples in 38 classes and notes that its copy is republished from Mendeley with the Background_without_leaves class removed. The repository itself does not expose an image-data license. Secondary catalogues/mirrors report inconsistent terms; no image archive was downloaded. Do not treat the 2016 paper license as image-data permission.
datasets.classMapNote: Exact 38-label order transcribed from TensorFlow Datasets 1.0.2 builder; do not assume this is the Kaggle derivative's folder enumeration without inspecting the archive.

datasets.name: New Plant Diseases Dataset (Kaggle augmented PlantVillage derivative)
datasets.license: Kaggle dataset license and per-file rights not verified. Underlying images substantially overlap PlantVillage and include offline augmentations; do not download/reuse until Kaggle terms and source rights are checked.
datasets.intendedUse: Potential training-pipeline reproduction and class-map comparison only; not independent new field data.
datasets.region: Primarily derived from PlantVillage; source image acquisition locations are not independently documented in the Kaggle listing reviewed.
datasets.imageTask: Leaf classification; augmented derivative of PlantVillage, not a distinct independent field dataset.
datasets.sourceAudit: Commonly reported as approximately 87,000 images across 38 classes with train/valid/test folders. Secondary analysis reports 54,305 source PlantVillage images plus 32,695 offline augmentations. These figures indicate substantial duplicate/near-duplicate leakage risk; deduplicate/group augmented variants with their source image. No archive downloaded.
datasets.classMapNote: Candidate 38-class set aligned to PlantVillage/TFDS labels; inspect the Kaggle archive's actual directory names and order before using model indices.

datasets.name: PlantDoc Cropped Dataset
classes: 27 reported crop/disease/healthy categories; verify exact folder names in archive
datasets.license: Repository declares CC BY 4.0, but README states images were scraped from internet search engines. Underlying third-party image copyright/permissions are uncertain; metadata only until image-level provenance and reuse rights are established.
datasets.intendedUse: Field-like external evaluation and possible classification research after image-level rights/provenance review; not a trusted ground-truth set by default.
datasets.region: India-focused research; images were internet-scraped and exact capture locations are not consistently documented.
datasets.imageTask: Cropped leaf-image classification; distinct object-detection variant exists and must not be mixed without task conversion.
datasets.sourceAudit: Repository README reports 2,598 images, 13 plant species and up to 17 disease classes; a 2026 Roboflow summary reports 27 total classes including healthy categories. The repo exposes a CC BY 4.0 license, but the authors describe annotating internet-scraped images, so the repository license cannot necessarily clear underlying photo rights. Annotation quality and original-source attribution require audit. No images downloaded.

datasets.name: PlantSeg in-the-wild disease segmentation dataset
classes: 115 plant-disease cases with pixel-level lesion masks
datasets.license: Zenodo record Rights section has a License heading but no value; reuse license is unverified. Do not download, redistribute, or train until license and image-level source terms are confirmed.
datasets.intendedUse: Separate lesion-localization/segmentation research and possible later evaluation of field symptom localization; not a drop-in image-classification dataset.
datasets.region: Multiple environments; 34 host plants according to the associated Scientific Data paper; individual image sources/regions must be read from metadata.
datasets.imageTask: Pixel-level lesion segmentation with masks; keep masks/task separate from image-level disease classification, severity grading, and object detection.
datasets.sourceAudit: Zenodo v2 reports more than 11,400 images across 115 plant diseases and a 3.0 GB archive. The current Zenodo Rights field is blank. The Nature Scientific Data paper describes metadata fields including image URL and license; these per-image fields must be checked before any reuse. No archive downloaded.

datasets.name: LeafNet and LeafBench multimodal plant pathology resource
classes: 97 disease classes across 22 crop species (LeafNet); LeafBench has 2,910 images and 13,950 QA pairs
datasets.license: Hugging Face metadata labels LeafNet data CC BY 4.0 and LeafBench MIT, but LeafNet includes public-source and in-house images whose upstream licenses may differ; datasets are gated and require contact-sharing consent. Per-image source rights remain unresolved. Metadata only; no image download.
datasets.intendedUse: Future vision-language assistant evaluation and symptom-reasoning benchmark; not a replacement for the compact image classifier or local expert-labelled dataset.
datasets.region: 22 crop species; 7 countries reported in dataset metadata; source-level geography must be inspected.
datasets.imageTask: Multimodal image-text classification and visual question answering; LeafBench QA labels are not simple classifier labels.
datasets.sourceAudit: The arXiv paper reports 186,000 leaf images, 97 disease classes and 13,950 QA pairs. Hugging Face dataset access is gated and requires accepting conditions/contact sharing. Public metadata reports roughly 70% public content; some images originate from other public datasets and retain upstream terms. LeafBench's own card describes 2,910 images and six hierarchical VQA tasks. Do not treat the dataset-card license tag or code license as automatically licensing every embedded image.

datasets.name: Citrus Leaf Disease Dataset (Zenodo V1)
datasets.license: unverified; Zenodo Rights field could not be independently confirmed
datasets.intendedUse: Metadata and aggregate metrics only until the source license and image rights are verified. No source images or derived model weights/ONNX are redistributed.
datasets.notes: Archive metadata reports 1,944 images in a classification archive with three filename-derived abnormal classes and no healthy class; a separate COCO/YOLO archive is a distinct detection task. The originating branch recorded an exploratory image-level 98.93% test accuracy, but weights and image-level manifests are withheld pending rights verification and the result is not Syrian field accuracy.

changeLog.limitation: Zenodo record-level dataset license and file terms remain unverified; no archive downloaded, no images copied, and no model training run performed.

changeLog.change: Flagged HERMOS source-count discrepancy between the Mendeley Version 2 landing page (914 images/13,904 labels), original 2022 paper (492/13,913), and 2026 package audit (492 image/XML pairs; 491 retained images; 13,765 usable regions).
changeLog.limitation: Actual archive not downloaded or inspected; do not assume the landing-page image count is the number of unique original field photographs.

changeLog.change: Added five user-contributed field leads for grape and lemon: spider mites, thrips, grape nutrient-deficiency chlorosis, citrus leafminer, and citrus leaf yellowing; attached extension references and diagnostic cautions.
changeLog.limitation: These are user-reported leads with no specified location, season, specimen, or expert confirmation. Yellowing remains a nonspecific symptom; no treatment recommendation or training label was created.

changeLog.change: Added user-contributed olive peacock spot (olive leaf spot) field lead with Mediterranean-relevant fungal disease references and symptom/latency cautions.
changeLog.limitation: The user did not specify location, cultivar, season, specimen, or expert confirmation. Record remains reported, not expert-confirmed; no image label, local prevalence claim, treatment recommendation, or training label was created.

changeLog.change: Expanded the nutrient-deficiency/chlorosis record from grapevine-only to a cross-tree-crop reference, with general woody-plant, fruit-tree, citrus, and tree-fruit extension sources.
changeLog.limitation: Nutrient symptoms and diagnostic thresholds remain crop-specific. Yellowing alone does not identify a deficient element; confirm with crop context and soil/leaf-tissue analysis. This broad reference is not a universal diagnosis or fertilizer prescription.

changeLog.change: Added a cross-tree marginal leaf necrosis/leaf scorch symptom reference following a user report for walnut and loquat; documented differential abiotic/root causes and distinguished the symptom from walnut blight.
changeLog.limitation: Walnut and loquat host associations remain user-reported leads, not independently confirmed diagnoses. Marginal scorch is nonspecific; no pathogen attribution, local prevalence claim, treatment recommendation, or training label was created.

changeLog.limitation: The dataset archive has not been downloaded or inspected; no images were added to training and no model was trained.

changeLog.limitation: No dataset archive has been downloaded, image-level rights/provenance and labels have not been audited, and no training or evaluation has been run. These datasets are not Syrian coastal validation data.
